extracted.intended_audience: aspiring parody songwriters, comedic musicians, and fans learning Weird Al's method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for creating parody songs that are musically faithful, widely recognizable, and comedically effective even for listeners unfamiliar with the source material. Covers song selection, musical recreation, lyrical technique, tone, and sustainment of a comic concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Rule: Funny independent of source familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody must be funny whether or not the listener is familiar with the source material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central requirement: the joke/comic concept must stand on its own for listeners who don't know the original song. This prioritizes broad comedic clarity over purely referential humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affectionate tone (poke not punch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Less biting and derogatory. 'More of a poke in the ribs than a punch in the face.' Affectionate, not contemptuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mean-spirited or contemptuous attacks on the original or its artist; aim for gentle, affectionate ribbing. Tone influences audience goodwill and long-term appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song selection: mainstream & culturally saturated
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the charts. Focus on songs with the biggest hits / most mainstream appeal. Cultural saturation = parody-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick songs that are instantly recognizable to the widest possible audience; mainstream hits give more listeners the immediate musical/rhythmic hook necessary for the parody to land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source study: meticulous analysis of original
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth study of the original. Meticulously analyze structure, rhythms, nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend time transcribing and internalizing the original's phrasing, rhythmic placement, and melodic nuances so the parody can mimic them precisely and still land the jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical recreation: faithful backing and re-performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep backing music identical to original. Transcribe by ear. Re-record from scratch (band re-performs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recreate the instrumentation and production closely so the source song is instantly recognizable; do not rely on cheap samplers or loose approximations if recognition is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept selection: sustained comic through-song concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick a concept that maintains humor through the entire song. Don't rely on a single joke. 'It has to feel like it could exist in that world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a premise broad enough to support multiple verses and callbacks; each verse should develop the comic idea and the chorus should repay/underscore the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyric construction: precise meter and phonological play
rubrics_metrics.description: Match syllable counts and stresses precisely. Sound substitutions (phonological play). Each verse develops the comic concept. Chorus repays the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the original's syllabic and stress pattern so lyrics flow naturally in the melody; use rhyme, alliteration, and sound-substitution to maximize comedic effect while fitting the meter exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody types: direct vs. style parody
rubrics_metrics.description: Two parody types: direct parody — same melody, new lyrics about a new subject; style parody — original song in the style of another artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose whether you're directly lampooning a specific track (requiring faithful musical recreation) or composing an original song that captures another artist's stylistic hallmarks (style parody enables more original composition while evoking an artist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity: use pop-culture details
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity — pop culture details make the parody feel grounded and funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, specific references (details, brand names, cultural touchstones) strengthen jokes and help the song feel authentic to its comic world; avoid vague, generic jokes that don't reward repeat listens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-listenability: songs must withstand multiple plays
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine a sustained concept, musical fidelity, and affectionate tone so listeners enjoy repeated hearings; avoid one-off gag songs that collapse after the initial laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rubric Checklist (verbatim)
rubrics_metrics.description:
1. Is the source song instantly recognizable?
2. Does the parody work even without source familiarity?
3. Does the concept sustain the full song length?
4. Are syllables matched precisely?
5. Is the tone affectionate (not contemptuous)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this five-question checklist as an evaluator's quick pass/fail assessment. These items map directly to song selection & musical recreation (1), the core rule (2), concept selection (3), lyric construction (4), and tone (5).
